CandidateInspection.description: The repository step: every version with the engine's verdict, or why none can run.

CandidateInspectionEvent.description: One event of an inspection's stream: progress, in order, then the inspection itself.

CandidateInspectionPhase.description:
What an inspection is doing, with how much of it is done: reading each file's GGUF header,
checking each version against this computer, then checking the drafters of the version it
recommends. A drafter total counts the drafter checks known so far, so it can grow.

CandidateInspectionProgress.description: How far an inspection has got, each version's verdict included as soon as it is known.

CandidateSource.description: Files not yet added: a Hugging Face repository at a commit, or a local directory.

CandidateVersion.description:
One version of a candidate. `download_bytes` is what adding it downloads before any drafter:
its files and the repository's projector, or nothing when it is already on this computer or
is a local file used in place. `catalog_model` is the catalog model this version exactly is (the
same repository, commit and file), installed or not: adding the version installs that model.

CatalogComponent.description:
A part of a catalog model's bundle that can be fetched on its own: the projector that gives
its target image input, or its separate drafter.

CatalogInstallationRemoval.description:
`kept_components`: the parts Magnitude stores for a model whose weights are found elsewhere
that the removal kept, because another model on this computer needs them.

CatalogMissingComponent.description:
A catalog component absent from this computer while the model's exact target weights are
found elsewhere. It is not an update: the model serves without it until it is fetched.

CatalogModel.description:
A catalog variant and its state on this computer. `aliases` are the `hf:` IDs its target's
files found in an external location (a Hugging Face cache) would have as custom models, which
clients resolve to this model, so references made before the file was attributed keep working.

CatalogModelState.description:
A catalog model's state here. `drafter_withheld`: it serves, and is assessed, without its
catalog drafter, which it doesn't fit with: it loads when it fits without it, and otherwise is
refused with its own shortfall. `stored_components`: the parts
Magnitude stores for a model whose weights are only in another app's location (its projector
package and drafter), which Remove deletes while the found weights stay and keep serving.

CatalogOptimizationProgress.description:
Kernel tuning after a verified download, in tuning work units. `Preparing` opens the device
and counts the units (0 of 0); `device` is the device a load would select, once previewed.

oneOf.description: Intended to be available as a supported catalog model.
Temporarily unavailable or not yet supported. Never installed or loaded.

Never offered for new installs and never loaded. An installed copy stays identifiable and
removable, and points at its replacement.

CatalogSupport.description:
What the release promises for a catalog model. It is independent of assessment, which says
what one device can do with it.

CatalogUpdatePart.description: What a catalog update brings: new model weights, a new projector (image input), or a new drafter.

top_k.description: Keep the `top_k` most likely tokens; 0 disables the filter.

ChatCompletionStreamEvent.description: A successful Chat Completions chunk or a post-commit OpenAI error envelope.

CountTokensRequest.description:
`count_tokens` takes only what renders the prompt; generation controls
such as `max_tokens` belong to Messages alone.

CustomModel.description:
A model on this computer that is not a catalog model. `drafter_pending`: its drafter choice is
automatic and its automatic drafter isn't worked out yet, so it has no drafter for now rather
than none. `update_commit` is set only for an added model whose repository's `main` has moved to
a commit where its target file has other content.

CustomModelDeclaration.description:
The persisted record of an added or imported model. For `Added`, `target` and `projector` are
repository-relative paths at the pinned commit; for `Imported` they are absolute file paths,
with the imported file first.

CustomModelOrigin.description: How a custom model came to be on this computer, which decides who owns its files.

DrafterCandidate.description:
One drafter a model may use. `automatic` says whether automatic choice may take it: the engine
binds it, the user didn't enter it, and with it the model still fits when it fits without one.
The first automatic candidate, in order, is the preselected drafter.

DrafterCandidatesResponse.description:
Drafter candidates for one target, in the product's category order. `entered` is the listed
reference the request's different drafter resolves to: a listed candidate that is the same file
(a catalog drafter by its package, otherwise the same repository, commit and path), else the
different drafter's own Other row; absent without a different drafter.

DrafterCategory.description:
Where a drafter candidate comes from, in the order automatic choice prefers: a separate drafter
in the model's own repository or folder, the matched catalog model's drafter, MTP heads built
into the model, then a drafter the user entered, which is never chosen automatically.

DrafterChoice.description: The drafter a custom model should use: the recommended one, none, or an exact reference.

DrafterPruning.description: Magnitude-owned drafter packages removed because no model uses them any more.

DrafterReference.description: A drafter's files, independent of which model uses it.

DrafterVerdict.description: Whether the engine binds a model's drafter. `None` means no drafter was configured.

ExecutionBackend.description: An execution backend compiled into the inference engine.

FoundSource.description: Where a scanned custom model was found.

GrammarTriggerResponse.description:
Lazy grammar triggers. The engine's grammars are never lazy, so responses
carry none; the shape remains part of the published contract.

HardwareAccessPath.description: An executor reading and writing a store directly, under its grant.

id.description: Index in this snapshot's access paths; placements reference this index.

HardwareDeviceId.description:
Stable cross-process identity of one execution device: the serialized Seismic device
selector (for example `metal:<registry-id>`, `cuda:<uuid>`, `vulkan:<uuid>`, `host-cpu`).

HardwareDeviceMemory.description:
Memory the OS does not manage, owned by one physical device. Its headroom
is what opened executors leave, which only a resident worker reads.

HardwareDiagnosticSource.description:
What a discovery diagnostic is about: one backend's enumeration, or the
OS's adapter interface (DXGI).

HardwareExecutor.description: One backend's handle on a physical device.

device_placement.description: The access paths device storage is allocated from, in order.

upload_placement.description: The access paths upload storage is allocated from, in order.

HardwareExecutorAvailability.description:
Whether an executor can run: with its device placement's stable fit, or
the reason it cannot.

HardwareGrant.description: What an executor's driver lets this process place along one path.

basis.description: The interface that reported the grant.

remaining_bytes.description:
What is left of the grant, where a reading without an opened
executor reports it.

HardwareHostRam.description: Host RAM, memory the OS manages, with what the OS reports of it.

available_bytes.description:
What the OS reports available to every program, before this
process's limits.

current_free_bytes.description:
What this process may still take: the OS's availability within every
process limit.

HardwareObservedStore.description: A volume, with the space the OS reports available to this process.

HardwarePhysicalDevice.description: One piece of hardware, with every executor that views it.

HardwarePhysicalDeviceId.description:
Stable cross-process identity of one piece of hardware: the serialized Seismic physical
identity (`host`, `registry:<id>` or `uuid:<uuid>`), which every executor viewing it shares.

HardwareReportedBy.description: The interface, and the figure of it, a reported value comes from.

physical_cores.description: OS-reported physical CPU cores, independent of process scheduling limits.

native_build.description: Engine build identity: engine version plus kernel bundle identity.

enabled_backends.description: Backends compiled into the engine build.

backend_diagnostics.description:
Backends that discovery could not enumerate on this machine, with the engine's own reason,
for example an absent driver. Empty when every compiled backend enumerated.

oneOf.description:
The executor the service's device selection takes: the one every load runs on. None when
no executor can run (each one's unavailability says why).

host_ram.description: Memory the OS manages; every machine has it.

volumes.description: The filesystems of the model store and the kernel cache.

HardwareStore.description: A place bytes live, and what the service plans against in it.

capacity_basis.description: The interface that reported the capacity.

stable_capacity_bytes.description: The capacity within process limits, less the planning reserve.

HardwareTransferPath.description: Bytes moved between two stores by an executor's copy mechanism.

HuggingFaceAccess.description:
What Hugging Face needs before it serves a refused repository's files: a signed-in account
(no token, or one it rejected), or that the signed-in account accept the repository's terms.

HuggingFaceCredential.description:
The Hugging Face token presented on every later Hub request; without one, Hub requests are
anonymous. It is write-only: no response carries it.

HuggingFaceModelSearchResult.description:
One repository. `unsupported` is empty for a repository whose architecture the engine runs,
else it names that architecture. `variant_of` is the catalog model whose shape fingerprint the
repository's GGUF has. `version_count` is how many GGUFs the repository's file list offers
(split shards counted once, projectors excluded), approximate since drafters are not told apart.

HuggingFaceModelSearchResults.description:
Results of every architecture, unsupported ones last; catalog and drafter repositories
excluded.

HuggingFaceRepositoryId.description: A canonical Hugging Face model repository (`owner/repository`).

native_build.description: Engine build identity: engine version plus kernel bundle identity.

backends.description: Backends compiled into the engine build.

IcnInstallationDeclaration.description:
Installation declaration written by the installer or the local build beside the installed
service. The service selects its execution device at runtime, so the declaration names no
backend; it binds the installation to one engine build.

IcnParentCommand.description: Private parent-to-child control; never exposed as a management HTTP endpoint.

KnownUnsupportedReason.description:
A reason the engine raises, typed where it raises it. `DraftArchitecture` is a separate drafter
whose architecture no drafter family binds, such as a Nemotron-H MTP file. `UnsupportedFormat`
is the service's own: a found model whose files are not GGUF, such as an Ollama model stored for
its MLX runner.

LocalModelRemoval.description:
The result of removing an added model's Magnitude-owned files. Files in external locations
are never touched, so the model may remain as found.

LocalModelsConfiguration.description:
The whole local-models configuration ACN owns and hands to ICN, at spawn and after every
change. Applying it is idempotent.

LocalModelsResponse.description:
`models` are the custom models to offer and assess; `hidden` are the ones the configuration
hides, listed so a client can unhide them, and never assessed. `unsupported` are GGUF groups
that cannot be read at all, and directories inside a location that cannot be read (the rest of
the location is still listed); a readable model the engine rejects stays in `models` with an
`Unsupported` assessment.

MemoryDomainId.description:
Stable identity of one store, a place bytes live: `system` for host RAM, otherwise the
store's own identity (a device's memory by its physical device).

oneOf.description:
Memory that cannot be moved is in the way of the load's claim in its limiting memory
domain. `available_bytes` is what a load may claim there: the reserve is already taken out.

A memory domain the load uses was under pressure: at its reserve, or with other programs'
memory being displaced faster than the system absorbs. No byte count describes it.

MemoryShortage.description: Why a model that fits the machine could not be given its memory.

oneOf.description: A fitting model, with one decode-speed estimate per requested depth.

The engine cannot execute a custom model, with every reason it found. A catalog model is
never unsupported: the pool drops a catalog target the engine cannot execute as a release
defect. An unreadable file has no serving profile.

ModelAssessmentDomainSnapshot.description:
One source's assessments. `Pending` until the source has been read (and, for custom models,
reconciled).

ModelAssessmentsSnapshot.description: Every model assessment in the service's one environment, established at service start.

ModelCandidate.description: A target (shards in order), projector and drafter, by paths relative to `source`.

tensorStorageBytes.description: Exact encoded tensor storage, when bounded GGUF inspection succeeded.

ModelFingerprint.description:
The shape a drafter binds to. Requantizations, finetunes and abliterations keep it, so it
matches a model to its parent catalog model when nothing else does.

memoryDomains.description:
The engine heap's observed standing per memory domain at the last observation. Memory is
elastic, so this is not a fixed reservation.

oneOf.description: The model fits this machine but could not be given its memory now.

fraction.description:
The load's completed fraction in `[0, 1]`, by measured work: tuning, when the load
tunes, is the first half and weight import the rest. Monotonic within a load; only
`Ready` means the load is complete.

instances.description:
Instances in lifecycle-update order, oldest first. The final matching
instance is therefore the current attempt for a model.

ModelLoadDevice.description: The execution device a model load uses.

contextWindowTokens.description: The engine-resolved supported maximum context: the serving ceiling.

requiredMemoryBytes.description:
The load's startup peak claim in the selected device's allocation domain (system RAM or
dedicated VRAM). It excludes future context growth, which is claimed as history grows.

ModelLoadStage.description: Where a model load is. The service's model instance status names the same stages.

ModelRoot.description: One resolved location ICN scans. ACN resolves the paths; ICN never guesses them.

PerformanceEvidence.description:
An estimated decode speed at one context depth: the model's bytes per decode step over the
device's memory bandwidth.

ProjectorVerdict.description:
Whether the engine binds a model's projector. `None` means the model has no projector; a
`Rejected` projector leaves the model assessed and served without it, taking text input only.

sliding_window_tokens.description:
Sliding-window attention span; 0 when every layer attends over the
full context, as in every family the engine executes.

SpeculativeMethod.description:
Native algorithm used by a speculative decoding stage.

Method and artifact packaging are intentionally independent. The enclosing speculative bundle
declares whether the selected method is embedded in the target or supplied by a separate draft
package.

StartModelDownloadRequest.description:
A bundle to download; `for_model` names the model the download serves, such as the model a
drafter is fetched for, and is echoed in every `ModelDownload` it produces.

oneOf.description: Enables reasoning with a hard reasoning-token budget.

sampler_ms.description: Time spent inside the sampler for this request.

parser_ms.description: Time spent incrementally parsing generated chat output for this request.

UnsupportedLocalModel.description:
A GGUF found on this computer that the engine cannot execute, or a directory inside a model
location that Magnitude can't read, which may hold more models.

UnsupportedReason.description: Why the engine cannot execute a model; a tag this contract does not name yet matches the unrecognized case.
